data_version.description: CalVer YYYY.MM.MICRO identifier for the data tarball (e.g. `2026.5.0`, `2026.5.1` for an in-month iteration); matches the GitHub Release tag `data-{data_version}`.

data_sha256.description: Deterministic SHA-256 tree hash of all data/**/*.parquet files. Recompute via `nucl_parquet.compute_data_sha256()`. PR CI gates on hash matching the on-disk tree; data_version must change iff data_sha256 changes.

additionalProperties.description: Two shapes supported: (1) evaluated cross-section libraries with `projectiles`, `version`, `path`; (2) external-dataset references (e.g. strata-data on HF) with `revision`, `fetcher`, `files`. The common required minimum is `name` + `data_type`.

projectiles.description: Light-ion shorthand (n/p/d/t/h/a/g) for evaluated libraries; heavy-ion identifiers (e.g. c12, fe56) for production / total-reaction libraries.

builder.description: Repo-relative path of the script that produced this library's parquets, or `null` if it was produced by a pipeline that is not in this repository (see #346). Required for every library that declares a `path`. Its digest is stamped into the library's manifest.json so a builder fix that never reached the data is detectable — see nucl_parquet/builder_stamp.py and #342.

provenance.description: Required when `builder` is null: what actually produced this library, established by research rather than assumed. Its absence means nobody has looked, which is a different state from 'we looked and the pipeline is not recoverable' — recording only `builder: null` conflated the two (#346).

status.description: `unrecorded`: no code that produces this library has ever been in this repository. `external-pipeline`: the producing pipeline is identified but runs outside it.

summary.description: One paragraph a reader can act on.

evidence.description: Commit shas, file paths and line ranges backing every claim in `summary`.

rebuild_path.description: What it would take to bring this in-repo, and what is unverified about that.

unverified.description: Claims in `rebuild_path` that were reasoned to, not checked — each stated so it can be settled by one probe. A structured field rather than an UNVERIFIED marker in the prose, because a marker in prose is a convention the next author drops.

rebuild_command.description: The literal command that re-ingests this library, rendered in the staleness failure message. `<scratch>` is a throwaway output directory; copy the result over `data/<library>/` afterwards.
